reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill, harness setup, CLI readiness and Doctor, README, TRUST, and domain terms for Codex, Hermes, and OpenClaw. Codex Notes can arrive at a PostToolUse boundary with the documented live-hook bootstrap limit, approval requirement, later-turn fallback, and acknowledgement duty. Hermes classic CLI hosts an exact-session attendant for Notes and post-consumption Answer Edits. Its attended plugin writer now also owns Question Routing for that exact live session, can interrupt a busy turn, and cannot cold-resume after exit; other Hermes surfaces remain unsupported. On macOS, the current OpenClaw Gateway generation attends its session and queues messages through a pointer-only followup with in-process context. Guidance requires acknowledgement of full context and explains that a crash may replay a pointer without context; such a pointer must not be acknowledged or automatically reinjected. Project Enablement, User guidance authority, Notification Request ownership, and transported-text authority remain unchanged.
